clue.text: Not even member gets cut into deal

indicators.note: something cut into another word is wedged inside it, splitting it apart

parts.note: a deal is a good buy, a purchase

explanation.surface: A club member is cut in on a deal that was not fair and even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' reads as a comment on fairness, but it is the definition: a surface that is not level.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpy road or surface is uneven, full of lumps rather than flat.

clue.text: Sweet-talks cavalry leader into mess

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: a botch is a mess, a bungled job

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

explanation.surface: Someone sweet-talks the head of a cavalry unit into making a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet-talks' looks like one verb, but the hyphen splits it: the definition is 'Sweet' and the wordplay starts with 'talks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard toffee-like confection made from butter and brown sugar.

clue.text: Hurry up and master preparation of the sake

indicators.note: a preparation is something mixed up and made ready, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A command to hurry and learn how to prepare the Japanese rice wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Sake here is the Japanese rice wine, which is warmed before serving.
explanation.definitionFit: To make haste is to move quickly, the idiom for hurrying.

clue.text: Long time before last train

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A long wait before the final train of the night departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about the time, but it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to want it intensely, the same as to yearn.

clue.text: When in Paris, young artist goes round in a state of confusion

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: A young painter wanders around Paris bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' is the convention for a French word. A quandary is the state of confusion you are 'in', so the surrounding 'in' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a perplexing situation where one cannot decide what to do.

clue.text: Tremulous setter's introduced into Queen's circle

indicators.note: being introduced into something means being put inside it

parts.note: Qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A nervous crossword setter is presented to the royal circle at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' is read as 'setter has', the setter speaking of himself as I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tremulous shakes slightly, as a quivering voice or hand does.

clue.text: Force to marry heartless rogue

indicators.note: a rogue element is wayward and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
without a heart means the central letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to wed a callous scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like the noun the bride must marry, but it is the anagram signal applied to what is left of 'marry' with its central R gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a military force, a body of troops.

clue.text: Dead EastEnder's first and last good man in soap

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead

indicators.note: the first and last letters are the outer ones, kept from each half of the compound

parts.note: the outer letters of each half of the compound name, East and Ender

explanation.surface: A late character from the EastEnders soap opera turns out to be the last decent man in the show.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in London. The first and last letters are taken from each half of the compound: ET from East and ER from Ender.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, here soap in the sense of a washing product.

clue.text: Extend library loan of rare Banks' novel

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its edges, the outer letters on either side

explanation.surface: A borrower keeps a scarce Iain Banks book from the library a little longer.
explanation.walkthrough: Iain Banks was a Scottish novelist, but 'Banks'' here points at the outer edges of 'rare'; 'novel' is the adjective, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew a library book is to extend the period you may keep it.

clue.text: Be determined to damn fake artist's work

indicators.note: something worked has been reshaped, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A critic resolves to condemn a forger's painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's work' reads as a painting; only 'work' is the signal, and 'artist' joins the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a firm stand is to hold a position resolutely, the idiom for being determined.

clue.text: After all, even shelters get vandalised

indicators.note: vandalised things are smashed up and broken apart, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A weary complaint that even the bus shelters are smashed up in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After all' looks like a sigh opening the sentence, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean in spite of that, conceding a point while maintaining another.

clue.text: Trained and hence improved

indicators.note: something trained has been shaped into a new form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Training leads, therefore, to getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: Enhanced means made better or increased in quality.

clue.text: Graze first of ewes on hilltops

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its top

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Sheep led by an ewe crop the grass up on the hilltops.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after: the letter from 'ewes' sits after the hilltops.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals browse when they feed on leaves and shoots, a synonym of grazing.

clue.text: Doubt wandering cousins receive letter in Greece

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, holding it inside
wandering means straying out of place, so these letters move about

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Relatives travelling around Greece are wary of a letter they are sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a feeling of mistrust, a doubt about someone's honesty.

clue.text: Can collapse into slight stupidity

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: to slight someone is to snub or ignore them

indicators.note: a collapse is a falling to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tin can crumples into a slightly silly state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to snub.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is lack of knowledge, which loosely equates to stupidity.

clue.text: Bright sign takes energy working long into dark

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day
E is the symbol for energy
a machine that is on is working
L is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: An illuminated sign needs power to keep going far into the darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon light is a glowing tube used for shop signs and advertising.

clue.text: Grind down shaft to fit between points

indicators.note: fitting between two things places the piece inside, flanked on both sides

parts.note: east again, the second compass point

explanation.surface: An engineer grinds a shaft so it slots between two points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' gives two compass points, both east, either side of the shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water grinds down rock.

clue.text: Dish allowed to be fixed up on 'ouse

parts.note: home with its H dropped, as a Cockney says it; the apostrophe shows the missing letter

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A meal one is allowed to rustle up in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means below: the other pieces sit under the dropped-H house, which mimics the Cockney 'ouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Omelettes are dishes of beaten eggs cooked in a pan.

clue.text: Oscar's told to keep away from the sea

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so it is the sound that counts

explanation.surface: A boy named Oscar is warned not to go near the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, the letter O and the word for avoiding make the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water, the open sea.

clue.text: Most squalid cave's briefly on site tour

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter is lopped off
a tour moves around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guide warns that the cave visited on the site tour is filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims the cave word by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotty is British slang for shabby or unpleasant; the superlative is the most squalid.

clue.text: Weep over girl's fruit

indicators.note: lying over something covers it on both sides here, wrapping around it

parts.note: the possessive pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone sheds tears over a girl's piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a small round red stone fruit.

clue.text: Bonus for person in film

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a background actor in a crowd scene

explanation.surface: A film performer is paid a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an additional item and also a non-speaking actor hired for crowd scenes.

clue.text: Baron's minion has key sign of a blow to the head

definitions.text: sign of a blow to the head

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for baron
a lackey is a servile follower

explanation.surface: A nobleman's servant has a key, implying a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is the musical sense, one of the letters A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: A black eye is bruising around the eye, the typical result of a punch to the face.

clue.text: Close opening to sinister chasm

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, as in heraldry

explanation.surface: Seal up the entrance to a threatening ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' means left in heraldry, from the Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split or fissure, a narrow chasm in rock.

clue.text: Car could be stretched to limit when it's out on circuit

indicators.note: with these two letters out, they are removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written, then losing two letters
a circuit is a round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A racing car might be pushed to its limit while it is out on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is not a pronoun here: those two letters are removed from the word before them.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine can be a stretch model, an extended luxury car.

clue.text: Ripping off bug from weed

parts.note: stinging is slang for swindling or overcharging
to nettle someone is to irritate them

explanation.surface: Tearing off an insect that came from a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' is the verb meaning annoy, not an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging nettle is a common plant with hairs that sting, widely treated as a weed.

clue.text: Photo of era basically shows characters raised without shoes

indicators.note: raised lifts the letters up, read from the end back to the start
showing characters means displaying letters already sitting in the words

explanation.surface: An old photograph of the period mostly shows people walking unshod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basically' looks like a comment on the photo, but only its first letter is used in the hidden string.
explanation.definitionFit: Barefoot means with bare feet, not wearing shoes or socks.

clue.text: Volunteers large number to divide ship's chores

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: dividing something splits it, so one piece sits in the middle of the other

explanation.surface: Many volunteers share out the jobs aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work to be done, the same as chores.
